convoLines.text: "Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days. It'll keep."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie."
"Still on needing to be alone!"
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "The whole fire was arguing about Nightlight last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Loud' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I sleep in short shifts instead."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the north treeline by the fallen oak and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Nightlight? Colin is pushing 'The Ugly Bastard'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
Rosa: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "The whole fire was arguing about Hushpuppy last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Bastard' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Okay. You don't have to have an answer."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can we talk?" Ivy sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." If we forget who we were, then what survived? Just bodies. I want more than that.
"Memory's a muscle. I exercise mine. The past is the only country I'm a citizen of."
"If we forget who we were, what exactly are we surviving for?"
"Still on what they want."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Hushpuppy? Colin is pushing 'The Loud Bastard'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember. Simple as that."
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"...Anyway. Sorry. What's on your mind? Anyway."
"We lost Colin and Ivy this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I keep turning over the last thing Ivy said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Still on what's been happening."
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We lost Colin and Ivy. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
The tension eases back to something ordinary.
"I sit apart to eat. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. DeShawn Hogan is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ DeShawn Hogan is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring DeShawn home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d12: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 55. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
burialWindowSay: d11: That night, they bring DeShawn home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d13: You say a few words for DeShawn. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d13: You bury DeShawn. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d14: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
